item.description: A pro-Palestinian group said it’s protesting businesses for supporting Israel. The Anti-Defamation League called it “antisemitic, plain and simple.”

media:content.media:text: A "boycott bike ride" against Pro-Israeli businesses in Philadelphia on Nov. 8, 2026, was met with hostility and arrests were
media:content.media:description: Three people were arrested Sunday as about 300 pro-Palestinian protesters clashed with roughly 200 pro-Israeli counterprotesters.

media:content.media:text: Bike riders, some wearing N95 masks with their helmets, passing by in a tight grouping.
media:content.media:description: The protest was organized by Philly Bike On Your Left, a group that describes itself as an “anti-fascist, anti-Zionist social cycling collective.”

media:content.media:text: The Philadelphia police attempt to separates the small group of boycott bike riders from the pro-Israel counter-protesters as
media:content.media:description: Philadelphia police officers worked to keep the groups separated as tensions continued to build before the bike ride began.

media:content.media:text: A billboard outside reads "Running over Jewish businesses isn't a peace plan"
media:content.media:description: Several officials, including Philadelphia Mayor Cherelle Parker and Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday took to social media to condemn the planned boycott.

media:content.media:text: Israeli and American flags are displayed on the sidewalk where dozens of people have gathered.
media:content.media:description: Half of the targeted establishments are owned by the Philadelphia restaurant group CookNSolo, whose Israeli co-owners have publicly supported and raised money for Israel.

media:content.media:text: A split American-Israeli flag on a pole outside a commercial building.
media:content.media:description: Some of the restaurants were seeing long lines of supporting customers.

item.title: Tensions rise in Philadelphia over boycott targeting Jewish restaurants
